title: Yosi Risha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Eikhah Rabbah, chapter 3, 17, relates that Rabbi Abbahu went to Botzrah and was received by Yosi Risha. He brought before him eighty kinds of birds’ brains and said to him: “Let the Rabbi not be angry with me, because I did not hunt much today.” Why is he called Yosi Risha? Because all his food consisted only of birds’ brains (from the word rosh, “head”). This is not Yosef Rishba, for he lived in the time of Rabbi, as explained in his entry.[^1]

notes.text: Hyman’s printed locator פ״ג־יז is retained, without calling it a typo or replacing it with modern paragraph numbering. The supplied Midrash Rabbah -- TE text contains this story in [Eikhah Rabbah 3:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Eikhah_Rabbah.3.6); the existing source note interprets Hyman’s 17 as the biblical verse, while Sefaria groups the passage differently. These systems are kept distinct. Botzrah transliterates בצרה without identifying a modern place. In שלא יכעוס רבי עלי, עלי means “with me” after “be angry”; it does not belong to the title Rabbi. Hyman’s distinction from Yosef Rishba remains his assertion, not an external identity merge.

The named Midrash Rabbah -- TE paragraph at Eikhah Rabbah 3:6 explicitly begins the episode רַבִּי אַבָּהוּ אֲזַל לְבָצְרָה, supporting the narrative title for Abbahu in this exact occurrence. Hyman’s other full רבי forms are retained as written, without adding a personal name or independently resolving his distinction from Yosef Rishba.
